body: Two statistical problems worth flagging. (1) The likelihood-ratio test in FR-005/SC-003 compares a regime-switching model against a single-regime VAR, but under the null the regime-specific parameters (transition probabilities, second set of coefficient/covariance matrices) are unidentified — the classic Davies problem. The chi-square null distribution does not hold, so a nominal p < 0.05 is not established; a bootstrap or information-criterion comparison would be needed. (2) SC-004 and SC-005 hard-code the substantive findings (regime-dependent autocorrelation, correlation shift of ≥ 0.20) as success criteria, which inverts the logic of the validated research question: the spec makes the null-hypothesis-rejection outcome a deliverable rather than an open empirical result, contradicting the validation section's own claim that 'the magnitude and sign of the correlation are empirical questions.' A related design issue: FR-003/FR-004 fit the HMM first, then estimate the RS-VAR conditional on hard regime labels; this ignores label uncertainty and makes the 'regime-specific' coefficients and their confidence intervals optimistic, since the same data informed the labels. A jointly estimated switching model or a label-simulation step would make the reported intervals honest.
